draft.title: Quadratic functions
card: A quadratic function is y = ax² + bx + c, with a ≠ 0. Its graph is a parabola. If a > 0 it opens up. If a < 0 it opens down. The y-intercept is c.
The axis of symmetry is the line x = -b/2a. The vertex lies on this line. Put this x-value into the function to get the y-value of the vertex.
The x-intercepts are the roots, where y = 0. Find them by factorising, by completing the square, or by the quadratic formula x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac)) ÷ 2a.
Example: y = x² - 6x + 5. The axis is x = 6/2 = 3. At x = 3, y = 9 - 18 + 5 = -4, so the vertex is (3, -4). Factorising gives (x - 1)(x - 5) = 0, so the roots are x = 1 and x = 5.
draft.remember: Axis x = -b/2a gives the vertex. Roots are where y = 0. The sign of a sets the direction.

a.q: What is the vertex of y = x² - 8x + 7?
a.why: The axis is x = -(-8)/(2×1) = 4. Then y = 16 - 32 + 7 = -9, so the vertex is (4, -9). (-4, -9) comes from a sign error in -b/2a.
a.clue: Find x = -b/2a first, then put it back into the function.

b.q: Mia studies y = -x² + 2x + 8. Which statement is correct?
opts: It opens down and has roots x = -2 and x = 4
It opens down and has roots x = 2 and x = -4
It opens up and has roots x = -2 and x = 4
It opens up and has a y-intercept of -8
b.why: Here a = -1, so it opens down. Multiply by -1: x² - 2x - 8 = 0, which gives (x - 4)(x + 2) = 0, so x = 4 or x = -2. Check: -16 + 8 + 8 = 0. The option with roots 2 and -4 has the signs swapped, and -4 gives -16 - 8 + 8 = -16, not 0.
b.clue: Check the sign of a, then set y = 0 and factorise.

b.best: It opens down and has roots x = -2 and x = 4
